title: How much of a foreign-currency receipt should a firm hedge?
decision: Decision: sell 0 %, 50 % or 100 % of a 10-million foreign-currency receipt forward for 90 days. Estimated quantity: the probability that the proceeds are below the budget of 11.4 million home units, and the expected proceeds.
reason: Exchange rates move with sudden jumps after news, and their returns have heavy tails. A VG process for the log rate gives these jumps with few parameters. The forward contract fixes the rate for the hedged part.
inputs: Spot rate 1.2 and forward rate 1.195 home units for each foreign unit. Log-rate parameters for each day: θ = 0, σ = 0.006, ν = 5 days. Receipt 10 million foreign units, budget 11.4 million home units. All values are illustrative.
dependence: The log rate change X is a VG Lévy process with stationary and independent increments. The rate in 90 days is S0 exp(X_T). The proceeds are h N F + (1 − h) N S0 exp(X_T). The model has no interest rates and no credit risk of the forward.
method: Exact sampling of the VG process at 90 daily grid times. The estimators are fractions and means over replicates. The mean log rate change has the exact reference θT = 0.
diagnostics: Reference value: drift = 0. Compare the shortfall probability with a Brownian model of the same variance. Other candidate models: a GARCH model, a regime-switching model, or the empirical distribution of 90-day rate changes.
interpretation: Without a hedge, the shortfall probability is near 0.18, above the limit of 0.05. A 50 % hedge gives about 0.04 and keeps most of the expected proceeds, so it is the choice in this illustration. A full hedge removes the shortfall but gives the lowest expected proceeds. Reject the model if the rate shows a trend or volatility clusters over the period.

data.text: Synthetic: illustrative spot and forward rates and illustrative VG parameters of an exchange rate. Illustrative values, not calibrated evidence.

dsl:
title: How much of a foreign-currency receipt should a firm hedge?
problem: A firm will receive 10 million units of a foreign currency in 90 days. The log exchange rate moves with jumps. Choose the hedge ratio with a forward contract.
param h = 0.5 "fraction sold forward"
param N = 10 {million foreign units} "amount to receive"
param S0 = 1.2 {home units per foreign unit} "spot rate today"
param F = 1.195 {home units per foreign unit} "forward rate for 90 days"
param budget = 11.4 {million home units} "budget value of the receipt"
param theta = 0 "drift θ of the log rate for each day"
param sigma = 0.006 "volatility σ for each day"
param nu = 5 {days} "variance rate ν"
X ~ variancegamma(x0 = 0, theta = theta, sigma = sigma, nu = nu, T = 90, steps = 90) {log rate change}
proceeds := h * N * F + (1 - h) * N * S0 * exp(last(X))
prob short = proceeds < budget "proceeds below the budget"
mean value = proceeds {million home units} "expected proceeds"
mean drift = last(X) "E X_T = θT"
alt "No hedge": h = 0
alt "Hedge 50 %": h = 0.5
alt "Hedge 100 %": h = 1
maximise value
require short <= 0.05
initial: X_0 = 0, the spot rate S0 today
dynamics: S_t = S0 exp(X_t), X_t = θ G_t + σ W(G_t), with G a gamma process of mean t and variance ν t (t in days)
focus proceeds

title: Which stop-loss level limits the trading loss best?
decision: Decision: set the stop-loss at a log-return of −2 %, −4 %, −6 % or −8 %, checked at each daily close for 20 days. Estimated quantity: the probability of a log-return below −8 %, the probability of a gap through the stop, and the mean log-return.
reason: A stop-loss sells at the first daily close below the stop level. A price with jumps can move from above the stop to far below it in one step. The VG process has jumps, so it shows this gap risk, which a continuous model does not show.
inputs: Log-return parameters for each day: θ = 0.0005, σ = 0.015, ν = 2 days. The rule checks the position at 20 daily closes. All values are illustrative.
dependence: The log-return X is a VG Lévy process with stationary and independent increments. The exit value is X at the first grid time with X ≤ −b, or X_T if no such time exists. The model sells at the close and has no transaction costs.
method: Exact sampling of the VG process at the 20 daily closes. The function first() finds the exit day. The estimators are fractions and means over replicates. The mean log-return without a stop has the exact reference θT = 0.01.
diagnostics: Reference value: ret = 0.01. The grid values are exact, but the model does not see the path between two closes. This matches a rule that checks only at the close. Other candidate models: a jump-diffusion model, or a model with intraday checks.
interpretation: A tight stop gives a small probability of a large loss, but it sells often and lowers the mean log-return. The stop at 6 % keeps the probability of a log-return below −8 % under 0.05 with the largest mean of the allowed levels in this illustration. Reject the model if the returns show volatility clustering or momentum after a fall.

data.text: Synthetic: illustrative VG parameters of a daily log-return and illustrative stop levels. Illustrative values, not calibrated evidence.

dsl:
title: Which stop-loss level limits the trading loss best?
problem: A trader holds a position for 20 days and checks it at the end of each day. A stop-loss closes the position at the first daily close below −b. Jumps can make the loss larger than b. Choose b.
param b = 0.04 "stop-loss level for the log-return"
param theta = 0.0005 "drift θ for each day"
param sigma = 0.015 "volatility σ for each day"
param nu = 2 {days} "variance rate ν"
X ~ variancegamma(x0 = 0, theta = theta, sigma = sigma, nu = nu, T = 20, steps = 20) {log-return}
hit := first(X <= -b)
pnl := if(hit > 0, X[max(hit, 1)], last(X))
prob stopped = hit > 0 "the stop-loss closes the position"
prob gap = pnl < -1.5 * b "exit loss larger than 1.5 b (a gap through the stop)"
prob big = pnl < -0.08 "log-return below −8 %"
mean ret = last(X) "E X_T = θT without a stop"
mean result = pnl "mean log-return with the stop"
alt "Stop at 2 %": b = 0.02
alt "Stop at 4 %": b = 0.04
alt "Stop at 6 %": b = 0.06
alt "Stop at 8 %": b = 0.08
maximise result
require big <= 0.05
initial: X_0 = 0 at the open of the position
dynamics: X_t = θ G_t + σ W(G_t), with G a gamma process of mean t and variance ν t; the stop reads X at the daily closes only
focus pnl
